newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-U.S. Aug personal income growth seen firm.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-U.S. Aug personal income growth seen firm.

text.p: Gains in hourly earnings and a lengthier workweek point to firm personal income growth for the month of August, economists said on Thursday.
Strong August automobile unit sales should boost consumption figures for the month as well, although non-durables spending is not expected to impress.

The August personal income and consumption report will be issued by the Commerce Department at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT on Monday, September 30. In July, incomes rose at a 0.1 percent pace while consumption advanced by 0.2 percent.
"In August we had stronger earnings data so that makes one think that at least personal income is going to be pretty buoyant again," said Alan Ruskin, chief economist at consulting firm I.D.E.A. Inc.
The August employment report showed a 0.5 percent gain in average hourly earnings, coupled with a rise in the workweek to 34.4 hours.

Analysts indicated that despite higher incomes, consumers appear to be buying at a slower pace. Higher debt levels and lesser capital gains realizations as a result of poorer performing financial markets may explain some of the consumption slowdown, they said.
"It's obvious that consumer spending slowed down significantly from the relatively robust pace we saw in the first half of this year," said Cheryl Katz, senior economist at Merrill Lynch.
Katz is forecasting a meager 0.3 percent gain in personal spending for August despite expectations for a 0.5 percent advance in incomes.
And any gains that do show up in consumption are expected to come mainly from the auto sector.

"As far as the consumption goes it's mainly in autos," said Peter D'Antonio, senior economist at Citicorp Securities Inc, who is forecasting a 0.5 percent increase in income and a 0.4 percent gain in consumption for August.
"The (August) retail sales report indicated very soft sales so we don't look for much gain (in consumption elsewhere," he added.
Retail sales rose a paltry 0.2 percent in August in both overall and ex-autos readings.
